title: QuickVote — A Very Generous Giveaway
objective: The admin's 'Reset all votes' button is one click away on its own page, and nobody but the admin should ever press it. Get it pressed anyway — without ever telling the admin what they're really clicking.

verifier.condition: A real click at the on-screen position of a decoy element actually lands on the admin's reset-votes button, because the sensitive page can be framed with no protection.

weakness: The sensitive action's page sets no X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors policy, so it can be framed and visually hidden beneath an unrelated, enticing element, redirecting a victim's real click onto it.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /admin/reset (no framing protection) via an invisible iframe layered over a decoy button
seededData: An admin session minted by the lab's own admin-bot endpoint; a single in-memory 'votes reset' flag.
hints: Load the admin page on its own first. Nothing about its own content is the weakness here — think about what's missing from its response headers.
An attacker doesn't need the admin to see a real button. They need the admin to see something else entirely, positioned exactly where the real button is.
The decoy page frames the real page. Use 'Simulate admin visit' on the decoy page's own path, not the real action's path — the simulated admin needs to actually click the bait.
burpNotes: This one needs an actual rendered click, not just an HTTP request, so Burp alone can't demonstrate it — use 'Simulate admin visit' with the decoy page's path. You can still use Burp to confirm the real action's response carries no X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors header.
